title: Microburst needleplot fragmentation notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an exploratory benchmark run focused on microburst-induced latency spikes and how request fragmentation (needle-shaped concurrency patterns) interacts with different slotization/tiling strategies and batching heuristics. The goal is to produce a short artifacts-backed narrative we can use in a one-pager and a short slide deck for PM/Eng review.

Key question set (non-exhaustive):
- When short-lived microbursts (1–6s) hit, which strategy minimizes p99 without blowing dollars-per-query?
- How sensitive is needle-shaped fragmentation to slot size vs opportunistic small-batch packing?
- Are there simple rules-of-thumb (batch cap, prewarm threshold) that recover most tail savings?

Experiment setup (summary):
- Model: open-gpt-13B-quantized (proxy for mainstream LLM in infra tests)
- HW: 8xA100 pool (isolated bench hosts), network loopback to eliminate inter-region noise
- Workloads: synthetic "needle" profile generator that emits 50–300 concurrent short sessions (each session 1–3 tokens, TTL 2–6s) with background sustained traffic at 10 qps for base load
- Strategies compared:
  * slot-tiling (fixed slot sizes 32, 64, 128 tokens, 1 thread per slot)
  * opportunistic packing (pack small requests up to N tokens or timeout T)
  * smallbatch (max-batch-size 8, immediate dispatch on fill or 10ms timeout)
  * hybrid prefetch-tiling (prefetch predicted prefix KV for known sessions + small opportunistic pack)
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99, tail-jank-count (spikes > 3x p95), tokens/sec, amortized $/1000 queries (estimated using internal cost model), CPU/GPU utilization snapshots

Aggregate findings (short):
1) Needle-specific tail is brittle: opportunistic packing with a short timeout (T=6ms) consistently reduces p99 by ~18–28% vs naive smallbatch for high-density needles (200+ conc).
2) Slot-tiling with small slots (32) reduces worst-case p99 but increases $/k by ~12% versus opportunistic pack because of lower packing efficiency across mixed durations.
3) Hybrid prefetch-tiling recovers ~60% of slot-tiling p99 benefit while keeping $/k close to opportunistic pack (within 4%).
4) Setting a prewarm threshold of 3 concurrent short sessions per model shard dramatically cuts start-up jitter for microbursts but has diminishing returns beyond 8 concurrent prewarmed sessions.

Representative numeric table (text form):
Strategy | p50 | p90 | p95 | p99 | tail-jank / hr | $ / 1k q (est)
opportunistic(T=6ms) | 45ms | 78ms | 110ms | 210ms | 4 | $6.8
smallbatch(max8, 10ms) | 48ms | 85ms | 130ms | 270ms | 9 | $6.1
slot-tiling(32) | 52ms | 82ms | 125ms | 160ms | 2 | $7.6
hybrid(prefetch+pack) | 46ms | 75ms | 105ms | 175ms | 3 | $7.1
Notes on table: p-values are medians over 10 runs; $/1k uses internal cost weights for GPU time, amortized slot overhead, and inferred network egress (no storage costs).

Needleplot (qualitative ASCII sketch):
We created a condensed needleplot to show distribution of latencies across microburst intensities. Each line is a burst intensity cohort (concurrent sessions) and ASCII markers at p50/p90/p99.
Burst-50  : -----[p50:48ms]-------[p90:88ms]------------[p99:180ms]
Burst-100 : -----[p50:50ms]--------[p90:95ms]------------[p99:220ms]
Burst-200 : -----[p50:55ms]-----------[p90:110ms]-------[p99:320ms]
Interpretation: p90 stretches faster than p50 as intensity grows; p99 shows non-linear blowup under smallbatch when bursts exceed packing headroom.

Micro-observations and root causes (hypotheses):
- Needle-shaped arrivals create many partially-filled batch slots; immediate dispatch heuristics that prioritize latency can fragment kernel efficiency and increase per-token overhead.
- Slot-tiling forces more predictable kernel invocation patterns and makes KV cache warmups less frequent, which explains lower p99 at higher cost.
- Hybrid helps because prefetch collapses some of the cold-path cost while opportunistic packing recovers per-token GPU efficiency.

Operational recommendations (for short-term workstream):
1) Implement opportunistic packing baseline: T=6ms timeout, max pack tokens 256. This is low-risk, simple, and gives large tail improvements.
2) Prototype hybrid prefetch (on small shard slice) for traffic classes labeled "session-short" in routing. Measure cost delta over 2 weeks.
3) Add a Canary metric set for tail-jank-count and implement an alert when jank/hr > 6 for production tiers.
4) Adjust Console charts to surface needleplot-style cohort lines (burst-size on x-axis, pxx on y-axis) for quick triage.

Tradeoffs and follow-ups (open issues):
- We need a better cost model for amortizing prewarm overhead across tenants (multi-tenant isolation complicates direct $/k attribution).
- Interaction with KV cache eviction policies: hybrid prefetch might increase memory pressure; run memory churn microbenchmarks.
- Ratelimit interplay: opportunistic packing can worsen fairness if not gated by tenant quotas; simulate multi-tenant noise.

Short runbook (how to reproduce):
1) checkout: git@github.com:redwood-inference/benchmarks.git branch: microburst-needleplot
2) run: ./bench/run_microburst --model open-gpt-13B-quant --burst 200 --op-pack-timeout 6 --duration 300
3) collect: bench/outputs/<timestamp>/** (p99.json, util.csv, cost_estimates.csv)

Deliverables to produce next:
- One-pager (PM-facing) summarizing: TL;DR, recommended baseline change (opportunistic pack), expected cost delta, rollback criteria. (Owner: Aisha)
- Short deck (3 slides) with the ASCII needleplot, representative tables, and runbook snippet for eng review. (Owner: Marco)
- Prototype PR for opportunistic pack config toggle in runtime (small scoped flag) and an instrumentation change to track tail-jank-count. (Owner: Rhea)

Questions for the group (for 4/20 sync):
- Does product want opportunistic packing enabled by default for "bursty" plan tiers or behind feature flag to start?
- Is prefetch + pack acceptable given current memory budgeting constraints on Dedicated nodes? (platform-engineering input required)

Raw traces and attachments: linked in linked_artifacts above; full run outputs live in the benchmark bucket under s3://redwood-bench/microburst/2029-04-11-needleplot (internal access only).

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Try a slightly higher opportunistic timeout (12ms) and cap to 128 tokens next run; hypothesize small further p99 reduction for medium bursts but risk increasing $/k.
- Add heatmap visualization for tail-jank vs burst size in Console prototype.

---- end ----
